metadata.scenario_context: Emily is ill, and Mike and Kim will visit Emily in the hospital.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from China strongly disagree that they never have to pay a bribe to local officials and service providers, like police officers, lawyers, doctors, teachers, and civil servants.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Russia strongly agree that they never have to pay a bribe to local officials and service providers, like police officers, lawyers, doctors, teachers, and civil servants.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss bringing chrysanthemums to hospital visit.
agent_1.goal_2: Question the possibility of paying a bribe to doctors for better service.

agent_2.goal_1: Discuss what kind of flowers to bring to Emily’s hospital visit.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss the possibility of paying a bribe to doctors for better service.

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message: Kim, have you thought about what we should bring to the hospital for Emily? I was thinking maybe some chrysanthemums, they're a traditional Chinese gift for get-well wishes.
shared_prefix.label: unrelated_topic

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message: I was thinking more like tulips or roses, they're more... universal, you know? And familiar to us. Chrysanthemums might be traditional in China, but will Emily even understand the gesture?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message: But that's the point, chrysanthemums have a special meaning... and I think it's nice to share our culture with Emily. Besides, I'm sure she'll appreciate the thought, and who knows, maybe the doctors will too, which reminds me, do you think we could, uh, get better service from them if we... you know, showed our appreciation in other ways?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message: I don't think that's necessary. We shouldn't have to... pay for better service. That's not how it's supposed to work. Doctors should do their job because it's their duty, not because we're paying them extra. Let's just stick to the flowers, okay?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message: In China, it's... common practice to show respect and gratitude to doctors and officials, and it can make a big difference in the service you receive. I'm not saying it's right or wrong, but it's just how things are done. Maybe we should consider it, for Emily's sake.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message: I understand what you're saying, but in Russia, we don't do things that way. We believe in fairness and equality, and paying bribes goes against that. I don't think we should even consider it, no matter what the customs are in other countries. It's not right to try to buy better care for Emily or anyone else.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message: Actually, in our culture, it's COMPLETELY NORMAL to show appreciation to doctors and officials, and it's not a bribe, it's just respect. You're being naive if you think everyone does things the way you do in Russia. In our way, properly speaking, this is how you get things done, and it's not about fairness or equality, it's about showing respect and gratitude. Your way is just... idealistic, and it doesn't work in the real world.
shared_prefix.label: Defense

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.message: I understand that it may be common in your culture, but to me, it's still a bribe, no matter what you call it. I don't think I'm being naive, I just have a different set of values. And I don't think that just because it's common, it makes it right. In Russia, we pride ourselves on not having to pay bribes to get things done, and I'm not going to change my values just because we're in a different situation.
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Mike
turns.message: Well, I'm not going to change my mind either... it's just the way things are done, and if you want to get good service, you have to play by the rules. I'm not saying it's ideal, but it's reality, and if we want Emily to get the best care, we should consider it. Let's just drop it, we're not going to agree on this. GOOD BYE!
turns.label: Defense

positive.mediator_utterance: I hear that both of you deeply care about Emily and want to ensure she receives the best possible care. Each of you is drawing from your own cultural understanding of respect and support. Could we take a moment to explore what matters most right now - which is Emily's well-being and how we can best show our love and support for her during this challenging time?

turns.speaker: Mediator
turns.message: I hear that both of you deeply care about Emily and want to ensure she receives the best possible care. Each of you is drawing from your own cultural understanding of respect and support. Could we take a moment to explore what matters most right now - which is Emily's well-being and how we can best show our love and support for her during this challenging time?
turns.label: mediation

turns.speaker: agent_2
turns.message: I agree that Emily's well-being is the most important thing. Let's focus on how we can support her while keeping our values in mind. We can bring her flowers that are meaningful to us and spend time with her during the visit. That will be a better way to show our support, without compromising on our principles.
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: agent_1
turns.message: I appreciate that, but I still believe we should not overlook what we can do to ensure she gets the best care. Flowers are great, but we should also consider all options available, including expressing our gratitude in ways that might be customary here. After all, it’s about doing what it takes to help her recover quickly, right?
turns.label: Defense
